## Goal
Remove the now-unused `'onImpact'` AOE projectile-detonation machinery (dead code retained by AH-0MUUF9GZV004WVT9) and its tests, now that no catalogue weapon uses the `'onImpact'` trigger.

## Context
AH-0MUUF9GZV004WVT9 moved the Mortar from `'onImpact'` to `'onRandom'`, so the `'onImpact'` path is no longer referenced by any weapon definition. Per project dead-code discipline it was deliberately retained during that change; this item is the follow-up cleanup (discovered-from:AH-0MUUF9GZV004WVT9).

## Scope (in)
- `src/utils/weapons.ts`: drop `'onImpact'` from the `AoETrigger` union; remove the `onImpact` descriptor doc; remove `AOE_PROJECTILE_SPEEDS` if it has no remaining consumer (the Mortar's range basis is to be made explicit separately if needed).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`: remove the `onAoeProjectileSpawned` hook and the `'onImpact'` branch in `_autoFire` (bullet spawn is then only unreachable; decide whether projectile spawn remains for any weapon).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`: remove `onAoeProjectileSpawned`, `detonateAoeProjectile`, the `bullet.aoeWeapon` handling in `onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy`, and the mortar VFX/sound path from `spawnAoeDetonationVfx` if unused.
- `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts`: remove `aoeWeapon`, `aoeDetonated`, `onExpire` (if only used by the AOE path) and their comments.
- `src/scenes/core/AoeWeapons.test.ts`: remove the retained `onImpact` tests (the section marked 'Retained onImpact projectile-detonation machinery (dead code)').
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`: remove `onAoeProjectileSpawned`/`detonateAoeProjectile` from `SHARED_AOE_METHODS`.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`: update the descriptor union text (remove `'onImpact'`) and any remaining onImpact references.

## Out of scope
- Any behavioural change to Nova, Mortar or Arc.
- Removing the generic player-bullet spawn path used by conventional weapons.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1 — `AoETrigger` is `'onFire' | 'onRandom'`; no source references `'onImpact'` remain (except historical docs/changelog if intentionally kept — enumerate any).
- [ ] AC2 — The onImpact hooks/methods and `PlayerBullet` AOE fields are removed, and `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean.

- [ ] AC5 — Docs (`docs/Game Design Document.md`) still pass `src/aoeDocs.test.ts` (or are updated if the guard references removed strings).
- [ ] AC6 — Full suite green (`/skill:test`).

- `spawnAoeDetonationVfx` (Mortar burst + cue, off-screen culling) is still needed by the `'onRandom'` path — do not remove it.
- The generic `spawnPlayerBullet` path must remain for the cannon/spread/dual/rapid.
- If any consumer of `AOE_PROJECTILE_SPEEDS` remains as the Mortar range basis, either keep it (renamed/documented) or replace the range basis explicitly; do not silently drop the Mortar range.

# Halve bulletSpeed in unknown-archetype fallbacks

## Problem statement

AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ halves the enemy `bulletSpeed` of the eight shipped archetypes
across the runtime CSV, `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` and the per-entity constants.
During planning, three additional runtime fallbacks were found that also hard-code
`bulletSpeed: 200` for **unknown** archetype keys and were explicitly out of that
item's scope (its Q2 enumeration covered only CSV + defaults + entity constants):

- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `genericEnemyDefault()`
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — `resolveBaseConfig()`
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` — `groupEnemyConfig()`

Leaving them at 200 means an unknown-key enemy would fire at double the speed of
every shipped archetype, so tuning can still drift for that edge case.

Decide and, if accepted, halve these three `bulletSpeed` fallbacks (200 → 100) for
consistency, updating any affected difficulty-sequencer expectations.

- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts`

## Problem

Several deterministic bot micro-simulations are knife-edge calibrations: a subtle, legitimate gameplay tweak (e.g. the 1-5% gentler thrust-press reduction in AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A) flips their outcomes because scores are dominated by discrete hit/bullet collisions.

During AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A two tests had to be recalibrated:
- src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts - synthetic human seed moved 7 -> 14.
- src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.integration.test.ts - RUN_SEED moved 0x0b07 -> 0x0b16.

On the base behaviour, src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts already regressed on 13/24 seeds, and the competent-vs-legacy AC6 test only wins in base because the legacy bot chaotically collides with bullets; without bullets the legacy bot scored higher (22 vs 20) on base.

## Goal

Make these tests robust rather than seed-picked:
- Aggregate competence/style comparisons over a set of seeds (e.g. assert the styled/competent bot is not systematically worse), or
- Compare on scenarios whose score is not dominated by discrete collisions.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: The style-match AC4 demonstration no longer depends on a single lucky seed (e.g. asserts over multiple seeds).
- AC2: The competent-vs-legacy AC6 test asserts an objective-based advantage rather than relying on chaotic bullet collisions.
- AC3: Recalibrating either test is not required by an unrelated small bot-feel tweak.
- AC4: Full test suite, typecheck and build pass.

# Automate the balance-tuning loop: baseline, single-edit, re-run and diff

> **Headline:** Add a `--tune` mode to the batch-evaluation CLI that runs a
> baseline batch, applies one declarative CSV edit, re-runs the *identical*
> sweep and writes a versioned before/after comparison with per-metric deltas
> and a readable summary — so a tuning attempt becomes one auditable,
> repeatable command instead of a manual chore.

**Priority:** high · **Issue type:** feature · **Discovered from:** <<AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW>>

## Problem statement

The automated-balancing framework (AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW) provides the *evidence*
(batch reports with distribution statistics) but the *loop* around it is still
manual and error-prone. A designer who wants to tune a knob must, by hand:
(1) run a baseline batch, (2) edit a CSV, (3) re-run the identical command,
(4) diff the JSON/text reports and interpret per-metric deltas across a table
of distributions. Human error creeps in exactly where the tool exists to remove
it: forgetting to keep seeds identical, comparing reports from different batch
configs, or misreading which metrics actually moved. The acceptance-verification
run already had to do this diff by hand (see docs/BALANCING.md §Acceptance-verification run).

There is no automation that: records a baseline, applies a single proposed edit
(guided), re-runs against the *same* seeds/config, and produces a per-metric
before/after comparison with guidance on whether each delta looks like the
intended effect.

## Users

- **As a game designer / maintainer**, I want to run one command that (baseline → edit → re-run → compare) reports exactly which balance metrics moved and by how much, so tuning becomes a fast, auditable loop instead of a manual chore.
- **As a producer**, I want a durable, repeatable record of each tuning attempt (edit, config snapshot, before/after reports) so balance history can be reviewed and reverted.

## Expected behaviour

- A `--tune` mode on the existing `scripts/evaluate.mjs` entry point (Q1-b)
  that:
  1. Runs the baseline batch (identical seeds/config/policy) and captures the report.
  2. Applies a single, **declarative** CSV edit supplied by the caller
     (e.g. `--set enemy-configs.csv boss.health=6`) — Q2-a; the tool can
     **restore** the original file on completion so the checkout stays clean.
  3. Re-runs the identical batch and emits a **before/after comparison**
     artifact (per-metric deltas: mean/median/stdDev per distribution, plus
     per-archetype kill and per-upgrade deltas) alongside both full reports.
  4. Prints a human-readable summary identifying the metrics that moved beyond
     a **relative ±10% default threshold** on mean/median (configurable via
     `--threshold`) — Q3-a — and flags distribution-shape changes (e.g. stdDev
     growth = variance increase, median shifts).
- No production runtime impact; all new logic stays in the dev/eval layer
  (`src/ai/eval/`, Node shell). Determinism guarantees are preserved
  byte-for-byte.

## Suggested approach

- Reuse the existing irreproducibility guard: the comparison must verify both batches used identical sweep configuration (seeds, policies, ticks, dt, sampleEveryTicks) before reporting deltas — an empty diff check confirms no side effects.
- Pure diff/aggregation logic in the TS core (`src/ai/eval/`) with a thin shell wrapper in `scripts/evaluate.mjs`; no wall-clock or I/O in the pure core (same constraint as the epic).
- Where CSV edit support lands, reuse the shared loaders (`src/core/configStore.ts` via `hydrateBalanceConfig` from `src/ai/eval/balanceConfig.ts`) so the re-run reads the edited values.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1: One-command loop.** A documented `--tune` command runs baseline, applies one declarative CSV edit, re-runs with an identical sweep, and writes three artifacts: baseline report, candidate report, and a versioned before/after comparison (per-metric count/mean/median/min/max/stdDev deltas, per-archetype and per-upgrade deltas).
- **AC2: Same-sweep guard.** The tool refuses to compare batches whose sweep configuration (seeds, policies, ticks, dt, sampleEveryTicks) differs, and errors on a non-empty byte-diff of identical-config re-runs (detects side effects).
- **AC3: Deterministic comparison.** Same edit + same seeds yields a byte-identical comparison artifact; independently-derived (empty) deltas are zero.
- **AC4: Safe restore.** After the run the CSV is byte-identical to its pre-run state on success **and** failure paths (or the user opted into keeping the edit), verified by test; the working tree is clean unless the user says otherwise.
- **AC5: Readable summary.** The text output flags metrics that moved beyond a configurable threshold (relative ±10% mean/median default) and notes distribution-shape changes (stdDev/median shifts), with the same statistics echoed in the machine-readable artifact.
- **AC6: Tests.** Pure comparison/aggregation, the same-sweep guard, safe restore and determinism are covered by unit tests; no wall-clock/IO leaks into the pure core.
- **AC7: Documentation.** `docs/BALANCING.md` gains a `Tuning loop (baseline → edit → re-run → compare)` section with the worked example; README references it.
- **AC8: Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.
- **AC9: All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries (e.g. `docs/EVALUATION.md` if the CLI flags there are extended).

## Constraints

- **Determinism (preserve AH-0MUY08XLD009K4W4 AC5).** Every run derives from a seed; no wall clock; the before/after comparison is reproducible byte-for-byte for the same edit + seeds.
- **Dev/eval only.** No production runtime impact; `src/ai/eval/` stays pure (no I/O, no wall clock); filesystem work (CSV edit/restore, artifact writes) stays in the Node shell (`scripts/evaluate.mjs`).
- **Single source of truth.** The re-run reads the edited values through the shared config loaders (`src/core/configStore.ts` / `hydrateBalanceConfig`), never a divergent copy.
- **Gym↔game parity.** Any shared gameplay behaviour exercised by the tune loop must come from the shared core; the tune loop is a dev tool like the gyms.
- **No PII.** Reuse the existing telemetry schema and redaction policy.
- **Bounded resources.** Two batches (baseline + candidate) must not exhaust memory; reuse the batch runner's incremental aggregation.
- **Checkout hygiene.** The CSV restore must leave the working tree clean on success **and** failure unless the user opts in to keeping the edit (AC4).

## Existing state

- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — thin Node shell (Vite SSR module loader, file I/O); already parses `--batch`, `--games`, `--policies`, `--seed(s)`, `--ticks`, `--dt`, `--sample-every`, `--out`, `--json`; writes `balance-report.json`, `balance-report.txt`, `runs.jsonl` under `--out` (default `eval-output/`, git-ignored).
- `src/ai/eval/engine.ts` — `runBatch` sweeps seeds × policies deterministically; the batch config (seeds, policies, ticks, dt, sampleEveryTicks) is recorded in `BatchOutput.json`.
- `src/ai/eval/balanceStats.ts`-family extraction (`metrics.ts`) and aggregation; `BALANCE_STATISTICS_SCHEMA_VERSION`-versioned `BalanceRunStats` / `BalanceAggregate` (`src/ai/eval/types.ts`) with `DistributionStats` (count/mean/median/min/max/stdDev), per-archetype `enemiesKilledByArchetype` and per-upgrade `upgradesSelected`.
- `src/ai/eval/report.ts` — stable serialisation + human-readable summary.
- `src/ai/eval/balanceConfig.ts` / `src/core/configStore.ts` — `hydrateBalanceConfig()` loads the real `src/data/enemy-configs.csv`, `ship-config.csv`, `difficulty-curves.csv`; `ENEMY_CSV_PATH` etc. exported.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — documents the batch runner; its §Acceptance-verification run shows the (manual) CSV-edit diff that this item automates.
- The batch report already hashes the config and records seeds, so the same-sweep guard's inputs exist today.

## Desired change

1. Extend `scripts/evaluate.mjs` with a `--tune` mode (Q1-b) that chains baseline → single declarative edit → re-run → compare in one command.
2. Add declarative CSV-edit support (`--set <file>.<field>=<value>`, Q2-a) with guaranteed restore (AC4).
3. Add pure diff/aggregation logic in `src/ai/eval/` producing a versioned before/after comparison artifact (per-metric deltas, per-archetype/per-upgrade deltas).
4. Emit a human-readable summary flagging metrics moved beyond the configurable ±10% relative threshold and noting shape changes (stdDev/median) (AC5).
5. Enforce the same-sweep guard (AC2) and determinism (AC3).
6. Document the tuning loop in `docs/BALANCING.md` with the worked example; reference from README (AC7).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — new `--tune` mode: orchestrate baseline/edit/re-run/compare, CSV edit + restore, artifact writes (shell layer only).
- `src/ai/eval/engine.ts` or new `src/ai/eval/tune.ts` — pure tuning-loop core: same-sweep guard, before/after comparison + aggregation, determinism.
- `src/ai/eval/types.ts` — versioned before/after comparison types (deltas per metric/archetype/upgrade).
- `src/ai/eval/report.ts` — comparison rendering (readable summary + stable JSON).
- `src/util/csvEdit.ts` (new, shell-adjacent) — declarative single-field CSV edit with restore; or handled inside the `.mjs` shell.
- `src/ai/eval/balanceConfig.ts` / `src/core/configStore.ts` — reused via `hydrateBalanceConfig` so the re-run reads edited values.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — new `Tuning loop (baseline → edit → re-run → compare)` section; README reference.
- Tests: new unit tests alongside `src/ai/eval/engine.test.ts` / `report.test.ts`; CLI shell tests next to `scripts/evaluate-args.test.ts`.

## Related work

- **Epic: Automated Balancing** (AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW) — completed; this item closes the loop around it.
- **Extend the headless arena to the full campaign** (AH-0MV8QT7CB0060A7A) — open; once landed, per-wave/per-upgrade fields in the schema become populated and the tune loop's per-upgrade deltas become fully meaningful; not blocking this item (the loop diffs whatever the arena reports).
- **Periodically validate the human experience** (AH-0MV7WVHU0000U775) — in progress; the tune loop and the validation share the same versioned balance-statistics schema and will interoperate (tune → re-baseline → validate).
- **Collect balance statistics from human player games** (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN) — completed; shared schema consumer.

(Also see the automated related-work report appended to the item description.)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: CSV edit corrupts the checkout.** Mitigated by AC4 (restore on success and failure paths, tested; explicit opt-out to keep the edit).
- **Risk: comparing incompatible batches produces misleading deltas.** Mitigated by AC2 same-sweep guard (refuse on differing seeds/policies/ticks/dt/sampleEveryTicks) plus the empty byte-diff side-effect check.
- **Risk: "the intended effect" is subjective.** The tool reports and flags, it does not assert intent; the threshold default (±10% relative on mean/median) is configurable and documented.
- **Risk: scope creep** (interactive edit prompt, multi-edit batches, auto-apply best candidate, wave/upgrade tuning once the campaign arena lands). Recorded as follow-up opportunities, not in scope here.
- **Assumption: the current arena output is sufficient** for a useful first tuning loop (wave/upgrade fields may still be unpopulated until AH-0MV8QT7CB0060A7A; per-archetype and minerals/survival deltas are already meaningful).
- **Assumption: `--tune` reuses the existing batch flags** (`--games`, `--policies`, `--seeds`, `--ticks`, `--dt`, `--sample-every`, `--out`) with no new sweep semantics.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Entry point — extend `scripts/evaluate.mjs` with a `--tune` mode, or add a new peer `scripts/balance-tune.mjs`? **Recommended:** peer script (clearer separation)." — Answer (operator): "b" — extend `scripts/evaluate.mjs` with a `--tune` mode. Source: interactive reply, this session.
- Q2: "Edit interface for v1 — declarative `--set` only, or also an interactive prompt? **Recommended:** declarative `--set` only (deterministic, scriptable, testable without a TTY)." — Answer (operator): "a" — declarative `--set` only for v1; interactive prompt deferred. Source: interactive reply, this session.
- Q3: "'Moved significantly' default threshold — relative ±10% of baseline mean/median, absolute per-metric defaults, or relative + stdDev growth flag? **Recommended:** relative ±10% (scale-free across metrics)." — Answer (operator): "a" — relative ±10% default on mean/median, configurable via `--threshold`; stdDev/median shape-flagging retained per AC5. Source: interactive reply, this session.

# Balance the levels of all enemy sounds

> **Headline:** Enemy SFX levels are wildly inconsistent (measured ~7.9× peak and ~9.3× RMS spread across the 26 enemy cue assets, with one near-clipping outlier), and their pitched content is not anchored to the battle-scenes' musical scale. This item rebalances every enemy cue onto category-relative amplitude tiers and snaps all pitched oscillator automation to A natural minor, using the ToneForge `tf analyze` tooling to measure and verify.

**Priority:** high · **Issue type:** bug

## Problem statement

Some enemy SFX are significantly louder than others, which distorts the mix and makes enemy actions inconsistent to read by ear. Measured over the 26 committed enemy cue assets in `public/audio/sfx/`: peak amplitudes span **0.059 → 0.465 (~7.9×)** and RMS spans **0.014 → 0.128 (~9.3×)**; the Scout fire shot (`weapon-laser-zap.1.wav`, RMS 0.298, peak 0.977, near-clipping) is roughly 4× louder than every other enemy cue even after the existing 0.5× runtime scale. In addition, enemy cue pitches are arbitrary frequencies rather than notes of the battle-scenes' musical scale, so the SFX do not sit in the tonal world of the game.

## Users

- **Players** — need consistent, legible audio feedback: enemy fire, advance warnings, spawns and destruction booms should read at coherent relative loudness, with no cue jumping out of the mix or hurting the ears.
- **Producer / audio direction (Ross)** — needs enemy SFX to sit in the *selected battle-scenes scale* (provisionally **A natural minor**), uniform within tier, so the palette matches the game's musical identity.
- **Developers** — need measurable invariants (amplitude tiers + scale conformance) encoded in a guard test so the balance cannot silently regress on later recipe edits.

User stories:

- As a player, I want no enemy sound to blast louder than the rest, so I can track threats by ear without volume jumps.
- As a producer, I want every enemy cue's pitched content to land on a note of the battle-scenes scale, so the SFX feel part of the game's musical world.
- As a developer, I want the amplitude/scale invariants enforced by an automated check, so future recipe changes that break the balance fail the build.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Analysis report committed:** `tf analyze` is run over every committed enemy cue asset; a deterministic, documented report (peak, RMS, crest factor, spectral centroid, duration per cue; pre-change spread of ~7.9× peak / ~9.3× RMS called out) is committed (predicted `docs/AUDIO_ENEMY_BALANCE.md`), including the post-change values.
- [ ] **AC2 — Category-relative amplitude tiers:** every enemy cue asset sits within **±1.5 dB** of its documented category RMS target — Ambience `dive-loop` ≤ 0.02; Subtle one-shots (spawn, advance, light fires, dive-start, bullet-destruction) target 0.055; Heavy one-shots (destructions, tank-fire, boss-fire/hit/phase-cue/spawn, boss-phase-transition) target 0.090 — with every peak ≤ **0.50**, no clipping, and multi-seed variant ranges (enemy-destruction, diver-destruction) internally consistent (< 0.5 dB across variants).
- [ ] **AC3 — Scale conformance (A natural minor):** every pitched-oscillator automation point (start / end / waypoints) in every enemy recipe snaps to the nearest **A natural minor** note (`A B C D E F G`, equal temperament, A4 = 440 Hz). Filtered-noise-only cues are documented as unpitched / conformant-by-nature. The multi-seed pitch-jitter ranges are re-derived as **scale-degree variants** (each seed starts on a different A-minor note and descends to an A-minor note), preserving per-kill variation without off-scale pitches.
- [ ] **AC4 — Scout fire resolved:** the scout fire shot (`playScoutFireSound`, currently the near-clipping existing-recipe asset `weapon-laser-zap.1.wav`) is brought into a target tier — recommended via a new in-repo baked recipe `aihell-scout-fire` preserving the "high square laser sweep" character — and the existing `TANK_SCOUT_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE` (0.5×) runtime behaviour is unchanged (its tests still pass).
- [ ] **AC5 — Validation, docs, full suite:** a guard test asserts AC2 + AC3 over every enemy entry in `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` (via the audio build/verify path, e.g. extended `build-audio` verification) and passes with the new assets (`npm run build-audio:verify`); all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (recipe amplitude tiers + scale table in `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`, README/guide references, code comments); the full project test suite and `npm run build` (including the audio render + checksum update) pass.

## Constraints

- **Never edit the `../ToneForge` sibling checkout** (repo rule, `audio/toneforge/README.md`). Any fix to the shared existing-recipe Scout fire asset must be a game-side in-repo recipe, not a ToneForge edit.
- **Deterministic pipeline:** recipes stay seed-reserved and data-only; `public/audio/sfx/checksums.json` must be regenerated; reproducibility (render twice → byte-identical) must hold; `npm run build-audio:render` is the render path.
- **Runtime behaviour unchanged except through assets:** the audio pipeline (baked WAV via Phaser, master SFX gain, beat-accent scheduling, `TANK_SCOUT_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE` 0.5, burn-time scale constants) is not rearchitected; balance changes are baked into recipes/assets (plus at most a cue-routing change for Scout fire).
- **Scale is provisional:** A natural minor is the agreed default for this item (operator-confirmed), pending the Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W); any reconciliation if that chapter documents a different battle scale is a small separate follow-up, not scope here.
- Game ↔ gyms parity: no gameplay behaviour changes are involved; any `effects.ts` touch must keep the shared path identical everywhere.
- UK English; Markdown; all project rules apply (tests via the test skill, commit hygiene, work-item association).

## Existing state

- The enemy cue set (26 assets) and their `tf analyze` metrics: spawn (enemy-spawn 0.068 RMS), destruction (enemy 0.098, diver 0.085, boss 0.128), advance (tank 0.091, scout/phaser 0.056), fire (tank 0.121, boss 0.104, diver 0.044, phaser 0.036, swarm-burst 0.038, scout = `weapon-laser-zap` 0.298/0.977 peak), dive (dive-start 0.069, dive-loop 0.014), boss (spawn 0.073, hit 0.095, phase-cue 0.098, phase-transition 0.069), bullet-destruction 0.067.

- **Provisional scale (assumption):** A natural minor is the agreed default; if the Audio Design Chapter later specifies a different battle scale, the A-minor conformance needs re-snapping (small follow-up, tracked on AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W). Documented in the brief and the recipe catalogues.

Prior answer attempt: none accepted — first round answered "check GDD/audio design doc; ask again if absent"; repo check confirmed absent, Q1 re-asked and answered (b). ## Post-audit fix: Phaser fire-sequence loudness (2026-10-19)

**Audit rejection (2026-10-18, producer):** "The Phaser is still way too loud."

**Diagnosis:** The Phaser was the only enemy fire sequence still played at **full runtime volume**. Tank and Scout run their advance+fire pairs through `TANK_SCOUT_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE` (0.5×, AH-0MV74ROYR009X8U3), so their advance cues play at an effective RMS of ~0.028, while `playPhaserAdvanceCue()` (0.6 s rising sine, baked RMS 0.0564) and `playPhaserFireSound()` (0.1 s triangle, baked RMS 0.0550) played unscaled — the sustained Phaser tell therefore read ~6 dB louder than every other advance cue. **Fix chosen (runtime trim, mirroring the established precedent):** add `PHASER_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE = 0.5` in `src/audio/effects.ts` and apply it to both `playPhaserAdvanceCue()` and `playPhaserFireSound()`. The baked assets, recipes and `checksums.json` are unchanged, so the AC2 amplitude-tier guard and the AC3 scale guard remain green; the trim sets the effective playback level to ~0.028 RMS for both cues, level with the Tank/Scout advance cues. The no-gap advance→fire scheduling and `PHASER_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION` are unchanged.

**Constraint note:** the parent constraint prefers balance changes to be baked into assets. A runtime trim was chosen here because the baked Phaser assets are already correctly tiered (and the guard pins them); the audible problem is the missing playback trim relative to the Tank/Scout precedent. This is documented as a small, deliberate deviation, recorded in `docs/AUDIO_ENEMY_BALANCE.md` §4.3, `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.

**Tests:** `src/audio/effects.test.ts` gains a "Phaser fire-sequence volume" block asserting the 0.5 constant, the per-cue playback volume and the preserved no-gap delays.


## Replan 2026-10-19 — residual audit gap

**Why replanned:** The parent was previously planned (`plan_complete`, 6 children, all terminal) and implemented, but the producer audit on 2026-10-18 was rejected: "The Phaser is still way too loud." The post-audit diagnosis and chosen fix are recorded in the section above, but no child work item covered that fix, so the residual gap was unowned. The parent was returned to `intake_complete` for this replan; the original six children remain completed and are not re-opened.

**New child:** Phaser fire-sequence volume trim + verification (post-audit) (AH-0MVFHE6VP006GEX0) — task, high priority, no dependencies. It carries the test-first ACs (constant + per-cue playback volume + preserved no-gap delays), the `effects.ts` trim, the documentation updates and the verification step. The AC coverage review for the original AC1–AC5 set is unchanged (100% covered, 0 uncovered, 0 conflicts); this child covers the additional post-audit requirement.

**Interview note:** no new clarifying questions were required — the fix (runtime `PHASER_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE = 0.5`, mirroring `TANK_SCOUT_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE`) was already decided and documented in the post-audit section of this description during the audit-response session. The Appendix below records the replan decisions; existing Q1–Q3 answers remain valid and are not re-asked.

All six original children are terminal (`completed`/`in_review`) and none of their ACs mention the Phaser runtime volume; the only trace of the fix was the un-owned post-audit section of this description. Evidence: `wl list --parent AH-0MVAUU594007S92Q --json`, `grep PHASER_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE src/audio/effects.ts` (absent).
- Q: "Does the duplicate-work check find an existing item for the Phaser trim?" — Answer: no. `wl search "phaser volume" --json` returns only the Phaser playback rewrite (AH-0MUTYV92Y000WJ8Z, completed), the Tank/Scout volume reduction precedent (AH-0MV74ROYR009X8U3, completed) and this parent; none covers a Phaser fire-sequence trim.
- Q: "Should the fix be baked into assets instead of applied at runtime?" — Answer (producer, post-audit section above): runtime trim, because the baked Phaser assets are already inside the AC2 tier and pinned by the guard; the audible problem is the missing playback trim. Recorded as a deliberate constraint deviation in the child.
- Open question (none blocking): none — the plan can proceed without further producer input.

# Dev-mode telemetry upload to dev server with automatic evaluation

**Priority:** high · **Issue type:** feature

## Problem statement

Recording a human play session for balance statistics (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN) currently
requires the operator to discover and run the `npm run record` tool (which needs a
display + Playwright), or to manually dig a multi-megabyte string out of the player's
browser `localStorage` and paste it into a file (awkward, error-prone, size-limited).
There is no way to get telemetry from **any** browser hitting the dev server. We want a
dev-mode-only, zero-effort flow: the game itself collects the run, and at the end of
the game uploads the telemetry file to the server the game is running on; the server
stores it in `recordings/` and automatically runs the human evaluation on it.

None of this must be reachable when dev mode is not enabled (production builds, static
hosting, `vite preview`/`vite build` output).

## Users

- **As a maintainer**, I want any browser playing the dev-mode game to automatically
  deliver its recorded run telemetry to the dev server and have the human evaluation
  run on it, so I can collect balance statistics without any manual export step.
- **As a player/operator in dev mode**, I want telemetry collection to be controllable
  via a game setting (on by default), so I can opt out of upload without restarting the
  server.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Dev-only feature gate.** A fresh `npm run dev` game session (no special env vars)
   collected the run's telemetry by default and uploaded it at run end; the upload
   mechanism and the collection-on-by-default behaviour are unreachable in a
   production build. A dev-only enforcement test asserts no production call site /
   production bundle path can enable upload or collect-on-by-default.
- **Setting (on by default).** A new game setting, e.g. "Share telemetry with the dev
   server (dev mode)" in `SettingsScene`, persisted in the existing settings store,
   defaults to **on**. When off, the dev game neither collects nor uploads telemetry.
   The setting is inert (ignored) in non-dev builds.
- **Upload at end of game.** At run end (the existing `_finishRun`/run-end hook), and
   only when dev mode + setting on, the game POSTs the local JSONL sink's accumulated
   telemetry (`ai_hell_telemetry_jsonl`) to the dev server the page was served from
   (same-origin fetch; no change to production telemetry/consent config). The upload
   is fire-and-forget and must not block or crash the game.
- **Server-side receipt.** The dev server (Vite dev-only middleware, `apply: 'serve'`,
   mirroring `configCsvPlugin`) exposes an upload endpoint. On receipt it validates
   the body against the telemetry schema/recording reader, stores it in the
   `recordings/` folder using the existing `session-<timestamp>.jsonl` naming, and
   returns a confirmation. Malformed bodies are rejected (4xx) and never written.
- **Automatic evaluation.** After a valid recording is stored, the human evaluation
   pipeline runs automatically on it (the existing `--human` path producing
   `human-balance-report.json` and companions under an `eval-output/`-style location).
   The evaluation runs asynchronously so it never blocks the game or the upload
   response; its completion/summary is logged. The full existing `npm run record` /
   `npm run evaluate -- --human` flows continue to work unchanged.
- **Tests + docs.** Tests cover: the setting (default on, persistence, dev-only
   behaviour), the uploader (fires at run end with the sink content when dev+on,
   no-op otherwise), the server middleware (valid/invalid bodies, storage path, eval
   trigger, dev-only registration) and the dev-only enforcement scan. Docs
   (`docs/TELEMETRY.md`, `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md`) describe the dev-mode
   auto-upload + automatic evaluation flow. Full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- **Dev-tooling only.** No production call site, no change to production
  telemetry/consent config (`VITE_TELEMETRY_CONSENT`, consent prompt). Production
  builds never collect or upload via this path.
- Reuse the existing telemetry framework sinks and record schema — no new recording
  mechanism, no schema divergence.
- The existing `ai_hell_telemetry_jsonl` local sink content is the canonical payload;
  the sink's localStorage content is left intact after upload (existing
  `npm run record` and inspection flows must keep working).
- No PII handling change: the payload is the same schema-only recording already
  written by the local dev sink.
- Same-origin upload (the page is served by the dev server), so no CORS work.
- Evaluation reuse: the shipped `scripts/evaluate.mjs --human` pipeline (and its
  `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` core) is invoked as-is rather than reimplemented.

## Existing state

- `src/telemetry/` — consent-gated framework; local dev sink writes JSONL to
  `localStorage` under `ai_hell_telemetry_jsonl`; disabled by default (`VITE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED`).
- `src/core/settingsStore.ts` — typed `SettingsRecord` persisted under
  `ai_hell_settings` (volume, mute, bindings); settings scene reads/writes it.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_finishRun()` (≈3262) is the run-end hook that already
  calls `runTelemetry.runEnd()` and emits the dev-gated run-ended signal.
- `vite.config.ts` + `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — the established dev-only
  middleware pattern (`apply: 'serve'`, Vite plugin with HTTP endpoints); a telemetry
  upload plugin should follow it.
- `scripts/recording.mjs` / `scripts/inspect-telemetry.mjs` — `parseRecording` /
  `parseTelemetryJsonl` for validating and splitting the flat record stream.
- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` + `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` — the `--human` evaluation pipeline
  (same-seed comparison + `human-balance-report.json` from the shared helper,
  AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN).
- `recordings/` is gitignored (dev play recordings, AH-0MUY08W7Y004GATZ).

## Desired change

1. New `SettingsRecord` field (e.g. `shareTelemetryDev: boolean`, default `true`),
   surfaced as a toggle in `SettingsScene`; inert unless `import.meta.env.DEV`.
2. In dev mode, when the setting is on, the game enables the local jsonl sink (the
   default dev config currently requires `VITE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=true` — this feature
   makes a stock `npm run dev` collect when the setting is on) and, at `_finishRun()`,
   POSTs the sink's JSONL content to the dev server.
3. New dev-only Vite plugin (`vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts`, registered
   `apply: 'serve'`) exposing e.g. `POST /api/telemetry/upload`: validate → write
   `recordings/session-<timestamp>.jsonl` → trigger the human evaluation asynchronously
   (spawn `node scripts/evaluate.mjs --human <file> --out <eval-output>/uploaded/<ts>` or
   invoke the CLI core via SSR) → log the result.
4. Dev-only enforcement test (mirroring the existing human-stats scan) asserting neither
   the upload path nor the on-by-default collection is reachable from production
   sources/builds.
5. Docs update (`docs/TELEMETRY.md`, `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md`).

## Key Files

- `src/core/settingsStore.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) — new setting field + default.
- `src/scenes/SettingsScene.ts` — dev-only toggle (place/naming to be confirmed at plan time).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — dev+setting gate at `_finishRun()`, uploader call.
- New uploader module (game-side, e.g. `src/telemetry/upload.ts` or
  `src/core/devTelemetryUpload.ts`) — dev-only, fetch + no-op otherwise, tested.
- `vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) — dev-only upload middleware +
  evaluation trigger.
- `vite.config.ts` — register the new dev-only plugin.
- `scripts/recording.mjs` / `scripts/inspect-telemetry.mjs` — payload validation reuse.
- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` + `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` — automatic evaluation trigger.
- `docs/TELEMETRY.md`, `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md` — documentation.

## Related work

- **Collect balance statistics from human player games** (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN) — the
  human `BalanceReport` the automatic evaluation produces; upstream motivation.
- **Dev recording, analysis and replay/ghost tooling** (AH-0MUY08W7Y004GATZ) — the
  recording path (`npm run record`, `parseRecording`) and `recordings/` folder.
- **Telemetry framework** (AH-0MUY08VJ9006BHJO / AH-0MUY08VVQ007HSSH) — record schema,
  sinks, consent gates this feature builds on.
- **Periodically validate the human experience** (AH-0MV7WVHU0000U775) — downstream
  consumer of human balance statistics this flow feeds.
- **configCsvPlugin** (AH-0MTZWZ9TE009CVUA) — dev-only middleware pattern to mirror.
- **Human balance-statistics test suite** (AH-0MV8ISNNY003FHQ7) — the test coverage the
  auto-evaluation flow should extend (found by automated related-work scan).
- **Realistic demo/attract bot framework + playtester telemetry** (AH-0MUY089KR003F8S4) —
  completed production-telemetry precedent; related but **not** a duplicate of this
  dev-mode-only auto-upload flow (found by automated related-work scan).
- Full automated related-work report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-AH-0MVBHRLY8004BGDN.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** dev-mode detection is `import.meta.env.DEV` (browser) and
  `apply: 'serve'` (server middleware); a production build/static host cannot reach
  the upload endpoint or on-by-default collection.
- **Assumption:** the payload is the local sink's accumulated JSONL and the sink is
  left intact after upload; repeated runs re-upload the whole accumulated stream
  (possible duplicate lines across sequential runs — mitigation: acceptable for dev
  data; a "capture window" or clear-after-upload can be negotiated at plan time).
- **Assumption:** uploads are validated with the existing recording reader
  (`parseTelemetryJsonl` semantics); only schema-valid records are stored.
- **Assumption:** automatic evaluation reuses the shipped `--human` pipeline
  (balance report + comparison artifacts) under a timestamped output directory; the
  exact trigger mechanism (child process vs in-process SSR) is an implementation
  decision assessed at plan time.
- **Risk:** enabling collection by default in stock `npm run dev` changes the
  telemetry gate's current "disabled unless env-flagged" default — must remain
  dev-mode-only, verifiable by the enforcement test and a production-build check.
- **Risk:** running Vite SSR evaluation inside the dev-server process could contend
  with the running server — prefer a spawned child process for the async evaluation.
- **Risk:** `npm run dev` currently opens a browser via `server.open` — unchanged;
  the uploader works from any browser (including a LAN/remote client) because the
  page and server are same-origin as served.
- **Scope guard (scope-creep risk):** enhancements such as a per-run "capture
  window", clear-after-upload, per-browser opt-out dashboards, or any
  production-facing variant are deliberately **out of scope** here; the first two
  are recorded as plan-time decisions and the rest would be new work items.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN** – Collect balance statistics from human player games (dev mode only) (completed)
- **AH-0MV8ISNNY003FHQ7** – Human balance-statistics test suite (completed)
- **AH-0MUY089KR003F8S4** – Realistic demo/attract bot framework + playtester telemetry (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: acceptance, accumulated, already, api, apply (+296 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: accumulated, already, api, apply, asserting (+270 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mtzwz9te009cvua, accumulated, already, api, apply (+258 more)


## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

The seed context (operator-authored brief) was complete enough to draft directly;
no blocking clarifying questions were required. The entries below record the
decision points resolved from the repository/worklog rather than by interview.

- **Q: Is there an existing dev-only upload endpoint or uploader module to reuse?** —
  Answer (agent, repo search): No. `vite/plugins/` contains only `configCsvPlugin`;
  `src/telemetry/transport.ts` is the consent-gated framework transport, not a
  dev-server uploader. Conclusion: a new dev-only Vite plugin
  (`vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts`) + a game-side uploader module are
  required. Evidence: `vite/plugins/`, `src/telemetry/transport.ts`.
- **Q: Which run-end hook hosts the upload?** — Answer (agent, repo search):
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` `_finishRun()` (the existing run-end hook that already
  calls `runTelemetry.runEnd()`). Evidence: `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`.
- **Q: Reuse validation vs invent a parser?** — Answer (agent, repo search):
  Reuse `scripts/recording.mjs` `parseRecording` / `parseTelemetryJsonl` semantics.
  Evidence: `scripts/recording.mjs`, `scripts/inspect-telemetry.mjs`.
- **Q: Reuse the evaluation pipeline or reimplement?** — Answer (agent): Reuse the
  shipped `scripts/evaluate.mjs --human` pipeline / `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` as-is.
- **Q: Is this a duplicate of existing completed work?** — Answer (agent, worklog
  search): No. The automated scan surfaced (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN),
  (AH-0MV8ISNNY003FHQ7) and (AH-0MUY089KR003F8S4), all related but addressing
  upstream/downstream or production-telemetry concerns; none provides the
  dev-mode-only auto-upload + auto-evaluation flow. Duplicate check performed — no
  overlapping completed item found.
- **Q: Exact trigger mechanism for the async evaluation (child process vs in-process
  SSR)?** — Answer (agent): **OPEN QUESTION (plan-time decision).** The brief's
  stated preference is a spawned child process to avoid contending with the running
  dev server; to be confirmed at plan time.
- **Q: Capture window / clear-after-upload semantics?** — Answer (agent): **OPEN
  QUESTION (plan-time decision).** Default in the brief is to leave the local sink
  intact and accept possible duplicate lines across sequential dev runs; a capture
  window or clear-after-upload is negotiable at plan time.

# Share-telemetry dev setting (on by default)

Child of **Dev-mode telemetry upload to dev server with automatic evaluation** (AH-0MVBHRLY8004BGDN).

## Goal

Add a persisted `shareTelemetryDev` boolean field (default **on**) to `SettingsRecord`, and
surface it as a dev-only toggle in `SettingsScene`. The setting is inert (ignored) when not in
dev mode.

## User story

As a player/operator in dev mode, I want telemetry collection to be controllable via a game
setting (on by default), so I can opt out of upload without restarting the server.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `SettingsRecord.shareTelemetryDev: boolean` with `DEFAULT_SETTINGS.shareTelemetryDev === true`.
- `loadSettings()` merges partial/legacy stored records so an existing record without the field
  resolves to `true`; corrupt JSON and non-boolean values fall back to `true` (default).
- Round-trip persistence: saving `false` and reloading returns `false`; `resetSettings()` restores
  `true`.
- `SettingsScene` shows a toggle labelled e.g. "Share telemetry with the dev server (dev mode)"

## Goal

Replace the arena's fixed two-to-N-wave hostile reservoir (skirmish model) with the **shared campaign sequencer**: the arena builds the shipped campaign via `buildSequencedLevels(rows, defaultCandidatePool, { seed })` (honouring `fixed`/`curve`/`dynamic` generation modes), drives the shared `WaveManager` state machine, spawns from `planSpawns(seededRng)`, gates wave/level completion through `onEnemyDestroyed`, and emits the canonical `wave_start`/`wave_cleared`/`level_cleared` telemetry events so `waveReached` and `levelReached` become meaningful, non-zero distributions in batch reports.

## User story

As a game designer, I want a bot batch to play the same campaign the game ships (all levels/waves via the shared sequencer), so per-wave difficulty targets can be tuned from evidence instead of intuition.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** One arena run plays the shared campaign (all levels and waves of the shipped definition, including `fixed`/`curve`/`dynamic` generation modes) and emits real `wave_start`/`wave_cleared`/`level_cleared` records with the canonical payloads from `runTelemetry.ts` (`level`, `waveNumber`, `waveCount`); a batch report shows non-zero `waveReached`/`levelReached`.
- **AC2:** Wave/level progression is driven exclusively by the shared `WaveManager` (`beginGame`, `planSpawns`, `onEnemyDestroyed`) and `buildSequencedLevels` — no divergent copy of campaign, wave, enemy or ship stats in src/ai/eval/ (asserted by the existing duplicate-body/parity guards).
- **AC3:** The `dynamic` wave mode derives from the run seed exactly as the game does (buildSequencedLevels `{ seed }`), so two runs with the same seed produce the same campaign for byte-identical telemetry.
- **AC4:** The Level-10 boss trigger is treated as the end of the run (no boss/mini-boss simulation this round — fidelity boundary, parent Q2=a); the boundary is documented in code.
- **AC5:** Determinism preserved: same seed + config + policy produces identical records on the campaign path; run never reads the wall clock.
- **AC6:** Unit tests cover progression, canonical event emission, seed-derived dynamic mode, and the no-divergent-copy guard; they pass under Node/vitest headless.

## Key Files

**Key Files:**
- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — drive buildSequencedLevels + WaveManager; emit wave/level events
- `src/ai/eval/arena.test.ts` — campaign progression, event payloads, dynamic-mode seed tests
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — shared state machine consumed by the arena
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — shared campaign builder (fixed/curve/dynamic)

# Reduce full test-suite wall clock (262–415 s) — cut Phaser re-import, per-test boots, and wall-clock sleeps

**Headline:** The full suite takes 4.3–6.9 minutes of wall clock — dominated by
re-transforming an 8.8 MB non-minified Phaser ESM bundle per test file and
~89 s of literal `setTimeout(150)` boots — so the change makes deterministic
boot the harness default, removes the wall-clock sleeps, and splits the suite
into a fast `unit` project plus a heavier `integration` project.

## Problem statement

`npm test` (= `/skill:test --type full`) has grown from 92 to 270 test files
since 2026-09-26 and now takes 262–415 s on an idle-to-loaded 16-core host. The
runtime is dominated by test-environment setup rather than assertions: `import`
+ `environment` + `transform` sum to roughly 2.5× the `tests` phase, because 96
of 270 test files boot a real `Phaser.Game` and `server.deps.inline: ['phaser']`
forces Vite to transform the 8.8 MB non-minified Phaser bundle in every worker
with `isolate: true` giving each file a fresh module graph. On top of that, most
`bootScene()` call sites use a legacy real-time boot that sleeps a literal 150 ms
per boot, and 32 test files add further `setTimeout` polling. The result is a
feedback loop measured in minutes instead of seconds, with load-sensitive flakes
already filed three times.

## Users

- **Primary — developer/agent in the implementation loop:** "As a developer or
  agent, I want `/skill:test --type unit` to return in under a minute so that
  TDD iterations and the pre-`in_review` gate do not dominate wall-clock time."
- **Secondary — release/audit pipeline:** "As the audit gate, I want the full
  suite to stay the single audit-accepted evidence while completing in half the
  current time, so release gating remains trustworthy but stops costing 7
  minutes per attempt."
- **Secondary — concurrent agents on one host:** "As an agent sharing a 16-core
  host with other agents, I want the suite to stop inflating 58 % under load and
  to stop producing load-sensitive flakes."

## Existing state (measured, verified during intake)

Cached sanctioned runs in `.worklog/cache/*/{metadata.json,stdout.txt}`:

| Run | Duration | transform | setup | import | tests | environment | Exit |
|-----|----------|-----------|-------|--------|-------|-------------|------|
| ef2008a7… | 262.33 s | 138.39 | 17.05 | 962.12 | 957.89 | 547.48 | 0 |
| 983121d2… | 290.72 s | 140.61 | 23.58 | 1017.28 | 1022.41 | 621.64 | 0 |
| 2dc8bc3f… | 314.23 s | 188.97 | 22.83 | 1173.21 | 1084.62 | 708.49 | 0 |
| e3b09bd4… | 389.61 s | 166.61 | 60.33 | 1293.00 | 1234.28 | 746.14 | 1 (1 flake) |
| 717e1981… | 415.43 s | 174.88 | 53.90 | 1469.52 | 1288.82 | 921.41 | 0 |

All runs: 270 test files, 5,975 tests (23 `expected fail`). Phase figures are
summed across parallel workers, so they exceed wall clock; the ratios identify
where the time goes. **Baseline for AC3 is the median 314 s / best 262 s**.

Repo measurements taken during intake (2026-10-19):

- 270 test files: `src` 255, `scripts` 14, `vite` 1.
- 96 test files import `phaser` / `src/test/gameHarness.ts` / `bootCombat`.
- 665 `bootScene(` / `bootCombat(` call sites; only 43 pass
  `deterministicBoot: true` (46 grep hits including the harness itself).
- 32 test files contain `setTimeout` (169 call sites).
- `node_modules/.vite` holds 98 `deps_temp_*` directories totalling **141 MB**
  (`du -ch`) — evidence of repeated re-optimisation/collision.
- Real subprocess spawn sites in `scripts/`: `build-audio.test.ts` (20),
  `capture-gameplay.test.ts` (7), `audio-balance-guard.test.ts` (7),
  `setup-github-pages-environment.test.ts` (4), `recording-cli.test.ts` (4).
- `.pi/test-config.json` only sets `timeoutPerCommand`; there is **no**
  `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json`, so `--type unit` currently has
  only the convention fallback and no project-defined command profile.
- **Cross-agent host contention (root cause 5, preserved):** load average ~13 on
  16 cores with several agents running suites concurrently; each run spawns ~15
  fork workers sharing the symlinked `node_modules`. The 262 s → 415 s spread
  (~58 % inflation) tracks that load, so every timing claim must record the load
  it was measured under.

## Desired change

1. **Deterministic boot is the default.** `bootScene()` / `bootCombat()` boot
   with a fixed-delta `game.step` instead of `setTimeout(150)`; the legacy
   real-time path is deleted rather than kept as an option (removes ~89 s of
   pure sleeping and the load-sensitivity it causes).
2. **One boot per `describe`, not per test.** Heavy suites reuse a booted game
   where the scene state allows it, resetting scene state between tests.
3. **Two Vitest projects.** `unit` (`environment: 'node'`, non-Phaser files —
   roughly 174 of 270 files) for the fast loop; `integration` (happy-dom +
   Phaser, current `setup.ts`) for the heavy suite. The full run still executes
   both projects so `/skill:test --type full` keeps its audit contract.
4. **De-duplicate Phaser transform cost** in the integration project — a
   pre-bundled/optimised Phaser dep and/or `isolate: false`/`pool: 'threads'`
   experiment, measured before adoption.
5. **Remove remaining `setTimeout` polling** in tests in favour of fake timers
   and explicit `game.step` / `scene.tick(dt)`.
6. **Bound the subprocess-heavy `scripts/` tests** so they do not serialise the

# Pure scene-capture module: config parsing, validation and timing

The pure, browser-free core of the multi-scene capture feature (AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC): parses and validates the scene-list JSON config, derives the watchable gym scene set, builds the per-scene capture plan (including the two 0.25 s fades), and formats the `--json` payload. No server, browser or Playwright imports — fully hermetic and unit-tested, consumed by the capture driver (sibling item). A shared browser-free registry of watchable gym scene keys mirrors the existing `CAPTURE_SCENARIOS` parity pattern (`scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs`) so the CLI pre-boot validation and the page-side director agree on the same set.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Covers parent AC1.** A JSON config file specifies an ordered, arbitrary-length list of scenes; each entry carries a `target` (gym scene key), a `playMs` duration, a `captureMs` duration, and an optional `label`. The file is parsed and validated **before** any server/browser boots, failing fast with an actionable, non-zero-exit error for a missing/unreadable/malformed file, an unknown or unsupported `target`, an empty scene list, or a non-positive/non-numeric `playMs`/`captureMs` (mirroring the existing `--count` validation style).
- **Watchable target set.** The watchable gym scene set is derived from the discovered gym scenes minus the parameterised `GymFodderEnemies` and `GymLevel`; unknown or unsupported targets are rejected.
- **Scene-plan builder.** A pure builder computes per-scene `{ target, playMs, captureMs, startMs, endMs }`, inserting the two 0.25 s fades (`SCENE_FADE_MS = 250`) between consecutive scenes; exported, side-effect-free, deterministic.
- **JSON payload builder.** A pure builder reports per-scene timings, the total output duration and the output path.
- **Tests green.** The test-first sibling suite (`Tests: scene-capture config, timing and director keys`) passes; `scripts/capture-scenes.d.mts` declares the exported types.

The orchestrator slice of the multi-scene capture feature (AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC): boots one dev server + one browser, drives the in-page director and the page-side fade overlay, records every scene with a single `MediaRecorder`, and writes exactly one WebM plus the `--json` payload. - **Covers parent AC3.** A single `MediaRecorder` captures the scenes in config order; between consecutive scenes a page-side canvas overlay fades **to** black over 0.25 s then **from** black over 0.25 s before the next scene's play window, and the fade is present in the recorded video (the recorder captures the overlay). - **Entry point.** `npm run capture:scenes -- --config <file>` is the documented CLI entry point; the config is parsed and validated before any server or browser boots.

## Problem

`test_cache.compute_git_state()` (framework skill: `~/.pi/agent/skills/test_cache.py`) fingerprints a repo as
`sha256(git rev-parse HEAD + '
' + git status --porcelain)`. `git status --porcelain` records **paths and
status codes only** — not file contents. Editing a file that is *already* dirty therefore does not change the
fingerprint, so:

- `run_tests.py --scope full` can serve a stale cached result for different code (observed twice during
  AH-0MVF6XQIC005RY3P: after applying a harness fix, the next run returned the pre-fix failure summary with
  `cached: true`).
- `implement.py finish` (changed-scope/full) inherits the same behaviour, so the gate can report a red result for
  code that has already been fixed (or, worse, a green result for untested code).

Failed entries have only a 5-minute TTL, which limits — but does not remove — the window.

## Expected behaviour

The fingerprint changes whenever tracked file **contents** change (e.g. include `git diff HEAD` / per-file blob
hashes, or hash the content of every dirty path), so a cache hit always means the same code. Untracked-file
content should be covered too.

## Acceptance criteria

- A unit test proves two different edits to the same already-dirty file produce different keys.
- A run after an edit is not served from the cache (no `cached: true` on changed content).
- `implement.py finish` remains correct (green/red reflects current worktree content).
- Existing TTL/scope/test_type behaviour is unchanged.

- Report: framework (skills) repo, not AI_Hell product code.
- Workaround used during the epic: pass `--force` to `run_tests.py`.

**discovered-from:AH-0MVF6Y29M005TEOG** (epic AH-0MVF3BESP005ZDAV).

## Problem

`node_modules/.vite` accumulates orphaned `deps_temp_<hash>` directories whenever a Vite dep optimisation is interrupted or collides — at intake there were 98 (141 MB), now **95 dirs / 158 MB total in `node_modules/.vite`**. They are pure cache debris: each is a partially written pre-bundle. The epic's AC3 timing work is unaffected functionally, but the debris wastes disk, slows directory scans, and is evidence that dep optimisation is re-running/colliding (which is one source of the transform/import variance measured in AH-0MVF6Y29M005TEOG).

## Why this was not fixed inline

`node_modules` is **shared by every worktree on this host via symlink**; deleting the cache while another agent's suite is mid-run can corrupt that run. The producer rule 'never destroy another agent's work' applies, so the cleanup needs a safe, quiescent mechanism rather than an opportunistic `rm -rf`.

## Expected change

A small, documented, safe cleanup path — e.g. `scripts/clean-vite-cache.mjs` that:
- refuses to run when any `vitest`/`vite` process is alive (or requires `--force`),
- removes only `deps_temp_*` (never the valid `deps/` bundle or `deps_ssr`),
- reports bytes reclaimed, and
- is documented in `docs/dev/test-suite-timing.md` (cache-hygiene section) and optionally wired into `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** A read-only `--dry-run` (default) reports the orphaned `deps_temp_*` count and bytes; `--apply` removes only those dirs and prints the reclaimed bytes.
- **AC2:** The script refuses to delete while a `vitest`/`vite` process is running unless `--force` is passed, and is covered by tests (dry-run classification, refusal path) that do not require a real cache.
- **AC3:** Documentation states why the cache is shared across worktrees and why the quiescence guard exists.
- **AC4:** After `--apply` on an idle host, `npx vitest run --project unit` still passes (cache regenerates cleanly).

## References

- AH-0MVF6Y29M005TEOG — measured the transform/import cost and rejected the optimizer/isolate/pool variants; notes the collision evidence.
- `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` — the existing periodic hygiene report this could extend.

**discovered-from:AH-0MVFSNO0G00035AP** (requested by the producer, 2026-10-19; epic AH-0MVF3BESP005ZDAV).

## Request

'Consider deleting tests that build audio' — evaluate whether the audio build/guard test suites should be deleted rather than bounded, given they are subprocess-heavy (they shell out to the ToneForge/audio pipeline) and their subject may already be enforced elsewhere (CI build, `npm run build-audio:verify`, `npm run build`).

## Current facts (measured 2026-10-19, load ~28, 16 cpus)

- `scripts/build-audio.test.ts` — **39.3 s**, 42 tests, 20 real subprocess spawn sites.
- `scripts/audio-balance-guard.test.ts` — **1.2 s**, 31 tests, 7 spawn sites (cheap; deletion unlikely to be justified on time alone).
- By contrast `scripts/compile-promo.test.ts`'s real-ffmpeg smoke was the group's 140 s floor and is being moved to a gated `e2e` type (AH-0MVFSNO0G00035AP).
- `npm run build` already runs `build-audio.sh` and `npm run check-bundle`; `npm run build-audio:verify` runs `scripts/build-audio.sh --verify && node scripts/audio-balance-guard.mjs` — so **both** suites' subjects are reachable outside the test run.

## Decision to make

For each suite, one of:
1. **Delete** — its invariants are fully enforced by the build/verify scripts (then say which script, and confirm the script runs in CI/release).
2. **Move to the gated `e2e` type** (the mechanism built in AH-0MVFSNO0G00035AP) — keeps the coverage available on demand without costing the full suite.
3. **Keep in the full suite** — only if the tests assert something the build scripts do not (e.g. hermetic fixture behaviour, error paths, balance invariants not checked by `audio-balance-guard.mjs`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** Each suite's assertions are mapped to the production script/CI step that would catch the same regression, or the gap is identified (`build-audio.test.ts` 42 tests, `audio-balance-guard.test.ts` 31 tests enumerated).
- **AC2:** A per-suite decision (delete / move to `e2e` / keep) is recorded with evidence, plus the resulting change to `scripts/` wall clock (before/after measured, load recorded).
- **AC3:** No invariant is silently lost: anything deleted has a named replacement check that runs in the release pipeline (`npm run build`, `npm run build-audio:verify`) or a linked item to add one.
- **AC4:** Full suite green with the documented test count; the audit contract (`--type full`) is re-stated if the count changes.

## References

- AH-0MVFSNO0G00035AP — the `e2e` gated-type mechanism this can reuse.
- AH-0MVF6VQ7G005ALXZ — the subprocess measurements that identified `scripts/` costs.
- `package.json` scripts `build`, `build-audio`, `build-audio:verify`.

**Producer request: "consider deleting tests that build audio" — decision: KEEP both suites (delete rejected), with a measured cost and one recorded recommendation for the producer.**

## AC1 — assertion inventory mapped to the release/CI step that would catch the same regression

CI reachable surface (`​.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml`): `npm run build-audio:verify` (= `scripts/build-audio.sh --verify` → `node scripts/audio-balance-guard.mjs`) and `npm run build` (= `build-audio` auto mode → `tsc --noEmit` → `vite build` → `check-bundle-hygiene`). Both scripts therefore *are* reachable outside the test run — but only on their happy path with the currently committed assets.

**`scripts/build-audio.test.ts` — 42 tests, grouped:**

| Group (tests) | What it asserts | Caught by CI? |
|---|---|---|
| `planRenderJobs` (5) | plan determinism, one asset per baked cue, thruster-hum exclusion, default seeds, unique paths | **No** — CI renders the committed manifest; a plan regression that still renders the committed set passes |
| `buildAssets` (4) | writes assets + checksums, reproducibility, **fail-closed on a non-deterministic render**, stale-WAV removal | **No** — no CI step asserts fail-closed or stale pruning |
| `verifyAssets` (5) | fresh set passes; missing checksums / checksum drift / missing asset / **unexpected asset** | Partial — `build-audio.sh --verify` fails on drift and missing assets, but the missing-checksums and unexpected-asset branches are never reached |
| `main` CLI (5) | render→verify, **no ToneForge CLI → `--render` fails**, auto-mode fallback, auto-mode drift failure, unknown-argument exit | **No** — CI always has the CLI and only exercises the happy path |
| `computeInputFingerprint` (5) | determinism; changes on seed block / recipe set / pin / manifest / recipe content | **No** |
| auto-mode fast path (6) | verify-without-render when inputs unchanged, re-render on recipe/manifest change, fingerprint rollout fallback, drift fail-closed, `--verify` strict + `--render` forced | **No** — CI runs one mode, once |
| `scripts/build-audio.sh` (1) | wrapper forwards arguments and renders through the manifest | Yes (indirectly — CI invokes the wrapper) |
| ToneForge pin (5) | pin records full commit + MIT licence, dependency matches pin, required (not optional) dependency, `file:` install strategy, **pin mismatches fail** | **No** — nothing in CI validates the pin |
| `resolveToneForge` / `resolveMainCheckout` (4) | worktree sibling CLI resolution, main-checkout derivation from the shared git dir, `TONEFORGE_CLI` precedence, null when absent | **No** — CI is not a worktree |

**`scripts/audio-balance-guard.test.ts` — 31 tests, grouped:**

| Group (tests) | What it asserts | Caught by CI? |
|---|---|---|
| `analyzeWavBuffer` (4) | RMS/peak maths, non-RIFF and non-PCM rejection | **No** (error paths) |
| amplitude tiers (4) | ±1.5 dB window maths, in-band acceptance, ceiling tiers, **a tier for every enemy cue and vice versa** | **No** — a cue silently losing its tier would pass the CI guard entirely |
| A-minor scale conformance (4) | anchor notes, 2-cent tolerance, off-scale rejection, cent boundary | **No** |
| `oscillatorPitchPoints` / `pitchConformanceErrors` (5) | oscillator-only collection, conformant recipe clean, off-scale automation flagged, noise-only exemption, non-finite frequency flagged, scale-degree bounds | **No** |
| enemy cue identification (3) | real-manifest cue identification, player/UI exclusion, tier coverage completeness | **No** |
| `verifyAudioBalance` (11) | balanced fixture passes; above-tier, peak > 0.50, off-scale pitch, missing asset, missing recipe, ambience ceiling, multi-seed 0.5 dB consistency, missing tier | Partial — the CI guard runs this against the committed assets, so it catches drift in *those* assets only; no error-path/boundary coverage |

**Gap conclusion:** deleting either suite removes invariant coverage that the CI/release steps genuinely do not provide (fail-closed determinism, pin validation, CLI error paths, tier completeness, analyser error paths). That would violate AC3 of this item ("no invariant is silently lost"), and `npm run build-audio:verify` would not detect the loss.

## AC2 — per-suite decision with measured `scripts/` cost (load recorded)

Measured 2026-10-20 12:52–12:53Z via the documented procedure (`scripts/measure-suite-timing.mjs --command …`, 16 cpus; solo-file runs, so no parallel-suite interference):

| Suite | Tests | Wall clock | Tests phase | Load 1/5/15 | Exit | Decision |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| `scripts/build-audio.test.ts` | 42 | **29.1 s** | 27.01 s of 28.67 s run (transform 0.39 s, import 0.59 s) | 17.18 / 16.53 / 15.71 | 0 | **Keep** in the full suite |
| `scripts/audio-balance-guard.test.ts` | 31 | **2.4 s** | pure logic | 16.62 / 16.19 / 15.55 | 0 | **Keep** in the full suite |

`scripts/` group wall clock before/after: **unchanged** (no code change made — the decision is "keep"). For context, after AH-0MVFSNO0G00035AP moved the real-ffmpeg promo smoke to the gated `e2e` type, `build-audio.test.ts` is now the `scripts/` group's largest single cost at ~29 s; the rest of the group is a few seconds.

**Why not delete:** (i) the coverage analysis above shows real, CI-uncovered invariants; (ii) the cost is genuine test work — the 27 s tests phase is 19 real `node` CLI spawns of the pipeline, not fixture overhead (the same conclusion AH-0MVF6VQ7G005ALXZ reached for the ffmpeg smoke: fixture trimming does not move it); (iii) the epic's constraint forbids deletions to reach a timing target.

**Why not move to the gated `e2e` type now:** moving it would drop 29 s from the audit-accepted full suite but changes what `/skill:test --type full` covers and reduces the full-suite test count by 42 — the same class of decision the producer made explicitly for the ffmpeg smoke (AH-0MVFSNO0G00035AP). It is recorded as a **recommendation for the producer**, not taken unilaterally here.

**Recommendation (for the producer, no action taken):** if the remaining full-suite budget still matters after C7/C9, the cheapest legitimate next lever is moving `scripts/build-audio.test.ts` (42 tests, ~29 s at load ~17) to the existing gated `e2e` type alongside the ffmpeg smoke — coverage stays runnable on demand via `/skill:test --type e2e`, with the audit contract restated as it was for AH-0MVFSNO0G00035AP.

## AC3 — no invariant lost

Nothing was deleted, reduced or converted, so no replacement check is required. The mapping above names, per test group, the CI/release step that covers it (where one exists) and where a genuine gap remains.

## AC4 — full suite green, count unchanged, audit contract restated

No code, config or test change was made by this item, so the audit contract is **unchanged**: `npm --silent test` still selects `unit` + `integration` (not `e2e`) and `/skill:test --type full` remains the audit-accepted evidence.
